title: Memory-Nonlinearity Trade-off across Quantum Reservoir Computing Frameworks
summary: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) harnesses driven quantum dynamics for time-series processing, yet the mechanisms behind the differing performance levels across its many implementations remain unclear. We show that apparently unrelated approaches-including memory restriction, weak measurements, operation near the edge of quantum chaos, and dissipative dynamics-are in fact governed by the same underlying principle, namely a tunable balance between memory retention and nonlinear response.
